original_excerpt:
From Felsenheld v. United States, 186 U.S. 126, 134 (1902):
"It is within the power of Congress to prescribe that a package of any article which it subjects to a tax, and upon which it requires the affixing of a stamp, shall contain only the article which is subject to the tax."   
From Felsenheld v. United States, 186 U.S. 126, 132–133 (1902):
Holding that under its taxing power, Congress has the authority to protect the administration and integrity of excise taxes by excluding all foreign objects, coupons, or promotional items from stamped packages of tobacco, regardless of whether the coupon itself is of negligible weight or value.
fidelity: Core quoted clause is in majority at 134 following 'We are of opinion that it ...'; capitalized standalone 'It' should be bracketed [I]t if strict transcription is intended. Paraphrase supports minute size/weight, not an express value exception.
pinpoint: 186 U.S. 132–134, quoted clause at preserved lines 328–332.
scope_note: Reasonable excise packaging regulation, not unlimited congressional power. Replace 'negligible ... value' with source's size/weight formulation.
